summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database transactionally backfills local message selector metadata from current message projections and retained canonical claims. Selector rebuild invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies.

schema.detail: Adds one local temporal header/pending table with fourteen ordered eligibility, reminder and retirement indexes, six source-change triggers and a metadata cut marker. Selectors retain only recipient, sender, canonical order, closed/reminder eligibility and cut intervals, never message bodies. Writes maintain changed selectors in their transaction; body-only changes avoid selector version churn. In isolated two-order 128-send/128-close bursts, selector maintenance added 0.476-0.603 ms send p95 and 0.482-0.720 ms close p95, with 50.05% additional send WAL and 77.62% additional close WAL. Existing cut-invalidation epoch and deletion/update/repair triggers remain. Earlier body version tables and their maintenance triggers are removed idempotently. Authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and shared projection digests are unchanged. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Fresh pages honor current desired-projection deletion: retained intent.desired claims do not restore removed message fields or recipient membership. Continuations require bounded server-issued metadata that binds the exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired and require restarting pagination. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: Initial selector backfill runs transactionally during Store open. On a fresh temporary copy of a checkpointed 118,390-claim, 9,712-message, 1.65-GiB database, open including backfill took 7.983 s, isolated header rebuild 2.679 s and populated reopen 23.418 ms; checkpointed database growth was 12.219 MiB and open WAL 13.041 MiB. These are API-only Store measurements, not live-daemon restart-to-API or rollout downtime proofs.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
